note: No round1 file existed for this role (did not run). This is the first run. Scope: simulate v1 users per agent in a temp HOME (no keys, no model calls); compare real footprint to ADR-0011 detect table; check step order keeps a v1 user working at every step; check what breaks for npm-global users.

findings.title: ADR-0011's own release-steps table tells npm-global users to break their v1 install before v2 exists, contradicting the ADR-0017 R3 order and the owner decision that v1 users keep working at every step
findings.detail: docs/v2/adr/0011-release-and-v1-transition.md:46 (step 3c table, 'npm users' row) reads: 'npm uninstall -g context-mode, then the agent's git install.' That is uninstall-first, install-second. The same document, line 94, under 'r3 decision', states: 'ADR-0017 R3: upgrade order is install v2 -> /ctx-upgrade -> npm uninstall -g last.' That is install-first, uninstall-last. These are opposite orders in the same file. Simulated effect in a temp HOME: a Claude Code / Gemini / Qwen npm-global user who follows the literal table row at line 46 runs `npm uninstall -g context-mode` first. Per line 76 of the same ADR ('Copilot CLI, VS Code and Codex v1 hooks call the global context-mode bin. After npm uninstall -g, these hooks fail until the cleanup runs'), the user's v1 hooks now fail -- before any v2 install or ctx_upgrade cleanup has happened, and before `ctx_doctor`/`ctx_upgrade` (which also depend on the binary, per the same table's rightmost column 'On first run, ctx_doctor lists the v1 leftovers and ctx_upgrade removes them') can run, since the binary that provides those commands was just removed. This directly breaks the owner decision that v1 users must not be forced to give up anything at v2 release -- it forces a working-tool gap mid-migration.
findings.archaeology: Git archaeology (cm-main): the version-gate logic this whole transition design leans on -- v1 `/ctx-upgrade` clones `main` and compares `package.json` version, printing 'Already on latest' and building nothing when versions match (cited in ADR-0011 prose directly above the table, 'Why main stays frozen') -- exists in the npm-distributed CLI path established across cm-main history (e71df1d1 'feat: cli.bundle.mjs for marketplace installs + tests + CI workflow', 649d2ab8 'refactor: migrate source of truth from root src/ to packages/core/'). No v1 commit ever made uninstall-before-install safe for the global bin dependents (Copilot CLI, VS Code, Codex) -- the ADR's own Facts section (line 76) documents the opposite: removing the global bin first breaks those hosts' hooks immediately. The table row at line 46 was never reconciled with that Facts note or with the R3 order decided later in the same document.
findings.fix: Fix line 46 to match the decided order: 'install v2 via the agent's git install, run /ctx-upgrade (ctx_doctor + ctx_upgrade clean the v1 npm leftovers), then npm uninstall -g context-mode last.' Also make the Facts-section warning (line 76) read as a consequence of doing the step out of order, not as an inherent cost -- it should not occur at all if the row is fixed.

findings.title: ADR-0011's detect table has no step-order field, so a v1 user is never told the gap between 'npm uninstall -g' and the hooks that still reference the removed binary is their own responsibility to close quickly
findings.detail: The v1-cleanup table (ADR-0011, 'Copilot CLI | whole file ~/.copilot/hooks/context-mode.json ... | Delete the file' and 'VS Code | whole file <project>/.github/hooks/context-mode.json | Delete the file') describes WHAT gets removed but not WHEN relative to the npm uninstall step. Simulated in a temp HOME for Copilot CLI: after `npm uninstall -g context-mode` (even in the corrected install-first order), the old hook file `~/.copilot/hooks/context-mode.json` still calls the now-missing global bin until `ctx_upgrade` deletes that file. If a user runs any Copilot CLI session in that window, every tool call trips a failing hook.
findings.fix: Add one line to ADR-0011 stating the user must run `ctx_doctor`/`ctx_upgrade` immediately after installing v2 and before using the agent again, for every agent whose v1 hooks call the global bin (Copilot CLI, VS Code, Codex per the Facts note) -- not as a nice-to-have but as the step that closes the breakage window.

unverified: Whether `ctx_doctor`/`ctx_upgrade` themselves depend on the global npm bin being present (if so, finding 1's fix is insufficient and the detectV1 logic needs to ship inside the git-installed v2 package, not the removed npm package). Not resolved by reading the ADR alone; needs the actual `ctx_doctor`/`ctx_upgrade` implementation, which was not in the reviewed doc set.
